responses_archetypeVariants.defender: This is the dodge the rest of the cluster imitates, in its purest form: not an argument, a diagnosis deployed to end the argument. Concede immediately that the arguer may well be depressed — many antinatalists are, denying it walks straight into the trap, and the concession costs nothing because it was never the point. You have not touched the asymmetry or the consent objection; you have changed the subject to the person holding them, and a syllogism's validity does not track anyone's serotonin. But the defender slot's real work is exposing the bad faith, because here it leaves fingerprints. The same interlocutor who says "get help" will, a few lines down the same thread, say "so why don't you kill yourself" — and those two sentences cannot be reconciled under a single motive of concern. They reconcile instantly under a single motive of hostility. The "care" is contempt with better public relations, and naming that is the move: not defending against the diagnosis, but pointing at the second sentence and asking which one was sincere. A boomerang is available and worth one pass — if emotional etiology discredits a belief, the natalist's life-affirmation is discredited harder, since it is the species-wide default, evolution-installed precisely to keep organisms reproducing, a far heavier psychological load than the minority dissent. But that only shows the principle is self-refuting when applied evenly; it does not prove antinatalism, because diagnosing the natalist's optimism would be the identical fallacy fired in reverse, and the slot does not get to spend the opponent's argument while keeping its own. Hold the honest remainder: roughly one deployment in a hundred is genuine worry, and that person gets met in good faith — but good-faith worry cashes out as a specific premise-level critique that points at the load-bearing claim and shows mood produced it, and the dodge never does that. Whether affect actually defeats the reasoning is a real and harder question — and it is the sophisticate's question, answered in that slot, not this one. The defender move stops where the bad faith is named.
